MachineryEquipment.title: Key Machinery and Equipment in the Port

gantryCrane.title: Gantry Crane - Container Lifting Crane at the Dock with Straight Travel
gantryCrane.content: Used for lifting containers on and off feeder vessels, capable of efficiently moving containers and easily positioning them as the containers are locked onto the crane arm and moved along the rails attached to the arm.

jibCrane.title: Jib Crane - Container Lifting Crane at the Dock with Rotating Function
jibCrane.content: Used for lifting containers on and off barge vessels, as the barge is a smaller vessel with a limited number of containers. The rotating container lifting crane is stationed at both of Sahathai Port’s barge docks, with one unit at each dock. Additionally, BBT has two rotating container lifting cranes at its barge docks.

rtg.title: RTG - Rubber-Tyred Gantry Crane for Container Yard Lifting
rtg.content: Designed for efficient space management, this crane allows containers to be stacked in multiple layers and ensures accurate placement, helping reduce costs and time spent in moving stacked containers.

mobileHarborCrane.title: Mobile Harbor Crane - Mobile Dock Crane
mobileHarborCrane.content: Sahathai Terminal strengthens its container handling capacity with one Mobile Harbor Crane stationed at the feeder port, working alongside the Gantry Crane during periods of high container handling volume. As it can move like a crane truck, it can flexibly relocate to support container handling at various points along the entire berth, ensuring fast, continuous, and highly efficient vessel service in every situation.

reachStacker.title: Reach Stacker - Container Lifting Truck
reachStacker.content: Our reach stacker can lift cargo weighing up to 42 tons, efficiently transporting containers within the dock area.

emptyContainerHandler.title: Empty Container Handler
emptyContainerHandler.content: Our terminal efficiently and quickly manages large empty containers.

tractorTrailer.title: Tractor and Trailer
tractorTrailer.content: Our tractors can quickly move containers, coupled with strong and durable trailers, ensuring safe transportation of containers throughout the journey.

forklift.title: Forklift
forklift.content: To manage goods efficiently, we have 13 forklifts to help handle goods within Sahathai’s warehouse areas quickly and safely.

docking.title: Berth Allocations
docking.content1: Shipping lines or their agents must email the details of the cargo vessel, services, and characteristics of the cargo vessel (general storage plan, ship securing plan, cold storage container placement plan, safety systems, and container space schedule) to Sahathai Terminal at least one week in advance before docking.
docking.content2: The shipping line or agent must send the long-term docking schedule at least one month in advance to Sahathai Terminal so that the terminal can plan the container booking in advance by 7, 3, and 1 day before docking. The shipping line or agent must also send an estimated docking date (ETA) and the approximate amount of cargo to be loaded or unloaded so that Sahathai Terminal can confirm the docking plan (POB) and the estimated departure date (ETD) of the vessel.

ResponsibilityScopeContent.content1: In the event that goods are damaged during container loading or unloading under Sahathai Terminal's responsibility, such as during lifting by forklift for transfer onto a truck, including any damage caused by Sahathai Terminal, Sahathai Terminal will be liable to the cargo owner or consignee for an amount not exceeding 50,000 Baht per item and/or 500,000 Baht per container.
ResponsibilityScopeContent.content2: In the event that goods are damaged and/or lost prior to being under Sahathai Terminal's responsibility, Sahathai Terminal reserves the right not to be liable under any circumstances.
ResponsibilityScopeContent.content3: Once Sahathai Terminal has delivered the goods in complete and proper condition, Sahathai Terminal shall bear no responsibility for any damage occurring after delivery.
ResponsibilityScopeContent.content4: Any person who signs the delivery form on behalf of the customer shall be deemed the recipient and responsible on behalf of the customer. Sahathai Terminal shall bear no responsibility for any loss or damage to the goods occurring after delivery to the recipient.

operatingHours.title: Operating Hours
operatingHours.content2: General containers transported by truck: 24 hours before Actual Time of Berthing (ATB)
operatingHours.content3: Reefer containers (fruit cargo): 1 hour before ATB
operatingHours.content4: Dangerous goods, Group 2 (DG GROUP2): transported directly from vessel/chassis to chassis/vessel
operatingHours.content5: Dangerous goods, Group 3 (DG GROUP3): can be stored at the port for up to 48 hours after being unloaded from the vessel, or 48 hours before the operating time of the Container Freight Station (CFS) at origin
operatingHours.content6: If overtime work is required, it must be notified before 16:00 on a working day
operatingHours.content7: CFS cargo cut-off time: 6 hours before the CY cargo cut-off time

CfsGoodsContent.title1: Sahathai Terminal accepts the following CFS/LCL cargo
CfsGoodsContent.content1_1: Goods packed in packaging or on pallets weighing no more than 2 tons, which can be lifted by forklift.
CfsGoodsContent.content1_2: For goods packed in packaging or on pallets weighing more than 2 tons, please contact our Customer Relations department to inform us of your request.
CfsGoodsContent.content1_3: Additional charges will apply if special equipment or tools are required for storing the goods.
CfsGoodsContent.title2: Sahathai Terminal does not accept the following CFS/LCL cargo
CfsGoodsContent.content2_1: Goods that may cause pollution at the port or warehouse, such as powder or molten chemical substances.
CfsGoodsContent.content2_2: Goods prohibited by government agencies, such as certain types of dangerous goods (DG).
CfsGoodsContent.content2_3: Heavy equipment, imbalanced goods, and other goods that cannot be lifted by forklift and/or require special lifting equipment.
CfsGoodsContent.content2_4: Sahathai Terminal reserves the right to provide additional equipment and personnel for special cargo handling cases. In such cases, the cargo owner must arrange their own lifting equipment and personnel.
CfsGoodsContent.title3: Regulations for goods packed in wooden packaging at the destination country
CfsGoodsContent.content3_1: If regulations regarding wooden packaging must be specified, customers must notify Sahathai Terminal at the time of booking.

RegulationsCargoShipsContent.content1: The ship's captain/chief officer is responsible for jointly inspecting Sahathai Terminal's property to ensure that no damage occurs from collisions when the cargo vessel berths, and throughout the time the vessel remains docked at the port.
RegulationsCargoShipsContent.content2: A gangway with appropriate handrails, as well as a safety net, must be provided as soon as the cargo vessel berths at the port.
RegulationsCargoShipsContent.content3: The ship's captain/chief officer is responsible for moving or repositioning the ship's crane whenever necessary to avoid obstructing port operations and to prevent collisions between the quay crane and the ship's derricks. Prior approval from Sahathai Terminal must be obtained each time before any movement or repositioning takes place.
RegulationsCargoShipsContent.content4: The ship's captain/chief officer is responsible for providing appropriate and effective lashing equipment. If requested by Sahathai Terminal, the captain/chief officer must inspect the lashing equipment to ensure it is safe and effective. If the lashing equipment does not meet standards, Sahathai Terminal staff must be notified immediately. Any delay or impact on operating time resulting from the lashing equipment inspection will require the shipping line's agent to pay additional charges.
RegulationsCargoShipsContent.content5: The ship's captain/chief officer is responsible for maintaining the safety of the cargo vessel, such as ensuring mooring lines remain tightly secured throughout the docking period.
RegulationsCargoShipsContent.content6: If crew members or other personnel wish to enter the port area, they must contact Sahathai Terminal's security department beforehand each time.
RegulationsCargoShipsContent.content7: Emission of smoke from the ship's funnel beyond the specified limit is not permitted.
RegulationsCargoShipsContent.content8: Discharging oil into the river or within the operational area is not permitted.
RegulationsCargoShipsContent.content9: Writing or marking within the port area is not permitted.

SafetyRegulationsContent.content1: Visitors are prohibited from entering the port area without permission from authorized Sahathai Terminal personnel.
SafetyRegulationsContent.content2: Visitors must contact the Terminal Service (TMS) office to receive and change into appropriate attire as provided by Sahathai Terminal, to ensure safety and that visitors are clearly visible.
SafetyRegulationsContent.content3: Visitors must comply with all prohibition signs, instructions, and warnings, and must wear a safety helmet at all times.
SafetyRegulationsContent.content4: Visitors entering the port area via the parking lot and/or boarding a cargo vessel must use the pedestrian walkway along the port perimeter fence and are prohibited from cutting through the container yard.
SafetyRegulationsContent.content5: Photography and video recording within the port area are prohibited without permission from authorized Sahathai Terminal personnel.
SafetyRegulationsContent.content6: All vehicles operating within the container area must not exceed a speed of 20 km/h on working days.
SafetyRegulationsContent.content7: All drivers within the port area must comply with traffic rules and safety regulations, and vehicles must not be left parked without authorization.
SafetyRegulationsContent.content8: Parking any type of vehicle that may obstruct traffic within the operational area is prohibited.
SafetyRegulationsContent.content9: All personnel must immediately notify Sahathai Terminal upon discovering any act that may affect safety within the port, or any act that may affect the port's infrastructure and security as defined under the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code.
SafetyRegulationsContent.content10: Violation of these regulations will result in revocation of the cargo vessel's permit.

HazardousGoodsContent.content: Hazardous goods are identified and classified using the UN Number. The goods can be divided into 3 categories as follows:
HazardousGoodsContent.link1: The UN Number can be checked in the system at

group2.title: Group 2
group2.content: Not accepted for storage (customers must pick up the goods at the side of the vessel only)

group3.title: Group 3
group3.content: Can be stored for up to 5 working days; customers must pick up within 5 days of the container being placed in the yard

group1.title: Requesting a Permit for Temporary Visits
group1.content: Visitors wishing to visit the office building or operational building must exchange their ID card and obtain a visitor permit from the security department at the port entrance gate.

group2.title: Requesting a Permit for Long-Term Visits
group2.content: Shipping line agents requiring a permit for long-term access to Sahathai Terminal must complete a request form and submit the documents to the Terminal Service office. Click here to send an email to the SSHE office at sshe.stt@sahathai.com.

group3.title: Access Rights to the Port Area and Cargo Vessels
group3.content: Personnel (other than shipping line agents) wishing to enter the port area or board a vessel must complete a request form, certified by the shipping line agent, in order to obtain Sahathai Terminal's permission to enter the operational area.

group4.title: Working Within the Port Area
group4.content: Personnel wishing to work within the port area must fully complete the Work Permit Form and notify the Terminal Service office. Click here to send an email to the SSHE office at sshe.stt@sahathai.com.

group5.title: Crew Members Wishing to Enter the Port Area
group5.content: Crew members wishing to enter the port's operational area must contact the security department at the port to register and exchange their crew ID card.

group6.title: Vehicle Stickers for Shipping Line Agents
group6.content: Shipping line agents requiring a vehicle sticker to access the office building must fully complete the vehicle sticker request form and submit it along with a copy of their driver's license and vehicle registration to the Terminal Service office. Click here to send an email to the SSHE office at sshe.stt@sahathai.com.

DocumentProcess.content1: The shipping line or its agent must submit information via EDI (Baplie)/CASP and a list of special cargo to Sahathai Terminal at least 12 hours before the estimated time of arrival (ETA). The shipping line must submit the ship's manifest, inbound container list, dangerous goods, and special cargo to Sahathai Terminal's documentation office.
DocumentProcess.content2_1: The shipping line or its agent must submit the Booking Forecast, Pre-loading Plan, and Special Stowage Instructions to Sahathai Terminal at least 12 hours before the estimated time of arrival (ETA).
DocumentProcess.content2_2: The shipping line or its agent must submit the Final Loading List, Final Loading Summary, and Final Loading Plan (if any) to Sahathai Terminal at least 12 hours before the estimated time of arrival (ETA).
DocumentProcess.content2_3: Once the cargo cut-off time at the container yard has passed, the shipping line or its agent must immediately submit the documents for containers awaiting loading to Sahathai Terminal to prevent delays.
DocumentProcess.content2_4: In the event that the berth is fully booked, the shipping line or its agent must submit the documents for containers awaiting loading to Sahathai Terminal to prevent delays.

BookingProcessContent.title: Container Yard for Export
BookingProcessContent.content: The shipping line or its agent must submit a "Pre-advise" to Sahathai Terminal's documentation office by email, EDI, or fax, containing the following container information:
BookingProcessContent.bullet1: Name of the cargo vessel and voyage number
BookingProcessContent.bullet2: The shipping line or its agent must submit the final customer name
BookingProcessContent.bullet7: Type of goods (general cargo, dangerous goods, reefer cargo, etc.)
BookingProcessContent.bullet8: Special conditions (such as temperature or the International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code)
BookingProcessContent.bullet9: The invoice or receipt must be prepared and submitted to the customs office at the entrance gate at the time the container is brought in by truck
BookingProcessContent.bullet10: For containers transported by barge, the barge controller will make a confirmed booking with Sahathai Terminal's documentation office before the barge arrives. The invoice must be submitted to Sahathai Terminal's documentation office before the container is brought in by barge
BookingProcessContent.bullet11: The shipping line or its agent must submit the CFS booking documents to the documentation office by email or fax
BookingProcessContent.bullet12: The shipping agent must submit the invoice/packing list before the goods are brought in
BookingProcessContent.bullet13: The shipping agent must submit the invoice before packing
BookingProcessContent.bullet14: The consignee must submit the Delivery Order (D/O) and customs documents to Sahathai Terminal's documentation office for domestic import containers
BookingProcessContent.bullet15: Sahathai Terminal's documentation office will prepare the delivery documents for storing import containers
BookingProcessContent.bullet16: The shipping line or its agent must submit the ship's manifest and notify the cargo status (CY/DIR/LCL/CFS) at least 24 hours before the cargo arrives at Sahathai Terminal

OCR.Title: Automatic Cargo Container Reading Technology (OCR)
OCR.Description: Sahathai Terminal has collaborated with domestic organizations to develop an automatic cargo container reading system, or OCR (Optical Character Recognition), for reading container numbers at the port entrance. The use of OCR technology enhances operational efficiency and smoothness, increases accuracy in verification, and reduces processing time, enabling customers to receive faster and higher-quality service.

FreeTradeZone.Title: Free Trade Zone
FreeTradeZone.Description: Sahathai Terminal understands the importance of having a customs office within the port area, which plays a key role in reducing time and costs for you.

FreeZone.Title: Free Trade Zone
FreeZone.Description: Located just 200 meters from Sahathai Terminal, with a total area of 6,400 square meters.

Facility.Title: Facilities
Facility.Description: Specially designed for seamless cargo handling through the terminal.

Fcl.Title: Cargo Storage Area
Fcl.Description: Dedicated storage areas for full container load (FCL) and free trade zone-specific areas.
